A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Reangle-A-Video work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary Appendices A–C. Matching content across pagination and section-number changes supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original static-view transport and dynamic-camera experiments, quantitative comparisons in Table 1, a 36-participant user study, and ablations in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments, user-study results, and ablations, and adds runtime results for alternative fine-tuning configurations in Appendix A.3.

M1.justification: Point-based warping, masked-loss LoRA fine-tuning, camera conditioning, and DUSt3R-guided inpainting remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2. The added hardware and frame-count configurations concern computational settings rather than a revised method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 28 Pexels/DAVIS-sourced videos and retain static-view transport, dynamic camera control, unseen-view generation, and appearance-edit scenarios. The additional 25-frame timing configuration changes temporal length within existing coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 and the corresponding qualitative and human comparisons retain Generative Camera Dolly and Vanilla CogVideoX for static-view transport, and NVS-Solver and Trajectory Attention for dynamic camera control. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Appendix A.3 adds timing configurations using an 80GB GPU without gradient checkpointing and a 40GB GPU with checkpointing and 25 frames. These supplement the original 49-frame, 40GB setup; the main benchmark protocol, metrics, training steps, and user-study design remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new fine-tuning-cost comparison examines runtime sensitivity to GPU memory/checkpointing and frame count. Existing analyses of stochastic guidance, warped-video training, masked loss, unseen views, appearance edits, and failure cases are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new runtime results are also point estimates without additional statistical reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the existing graphical results are unchanged. Appendix A.3 adds approximately 18 minutes and 3.3× speedup on an 80GB GPU without checkpointing, and 26 minutes and 2.3× speedup with 25 frames on a 40GB GPU. These are additional configurations relative to the retained approximately one-hour setup, not same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), warping and masking definitions, and the diffusion/flow sampling mathematics are retained. Appendix A.5 becomes A.6 without changing its mathematical content; no theorem, proof, or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: synchronized multi-view video generation from a monocular video using existing image/video priors, view-invariant motion learning, and consistent starting-image generation. The introduction's wording changes do not alter these claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of motion learning and generalization, and limitations involving depth/camera errors, small details, complex motion, latent compression, and scene-specific tuning remain unchanged. Checkpointing's backpropagation overhead was already explained in v1's Section 4.1 footnote.

D1.justification: v3 adds practical resource and timing information for the 80GB/no-checkpointing and 40GB/25-frame alternatives in Appendix A.3. v1 already disclosed the original checkpointing setup. Existing hyperparameters, model-checkpoint links, and code/data release statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 97 cited works and related-work positioning are retained. Changes to reference pagination and citation back-references do not add literature or redefine the relationship to prior research.

P1.justification: v3 lightly rewrites the introduction, adds a short fine-tuning-cost subsection, updates affiliations and funding acknowledgments, and corrects the broken method reference in Appendix B.1. Subsequent appendix subsections are renumbered, while the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1–15 and Tables 1–3 retain their content. Appendix algorithms and Table 3 are repositioned, Figure 15's caption is expanded, and text reflow changes the reference and appendix layouts. These are limited presentation changes without redesigned scientific displays.

improvement.justification: v1 already disclosed approximately one-hour fine-tuning and checkpointing overhead; v3's Appendix A.3 makes practical alternatives more concrete through hardware, frame-count, and runtime information. The corrected appendix cross-reference also improves navigation. The benefit is limited: faster configurations require more GPU memory or fewer frames, and quality equivalence for the 25-frame option is not established. The core method and validation remain unchanged.
